cleanIntro: The DEFCAN-556 and DEFCAN-762 are SEALED suppressors. CMMG says so in one sentence for both cans: the front cap and inner baffles are not meant to come apart, and nothing in this guide opens the body. What CMMG does publish is real maintenance on the outside of that sealed tube: the can off the host on its lever-lock QD mount, the HUB mount unscrewed from the body so its threads and the blast chamber can be cleaned and oiled, a bore brush with solvent but NEVER a patch, an optional solvent soak, and a flush routine for a can that has been in water. CMMG's interval is before and after every use. The two cans differ only in size and rating: the 556 is a 5.56x45mm can and comes with a 1/2-28 ZEROED SVD brake, the 762 is a .308 Win can and comes with a 5/8-24 brake. Fitting that brake to the barrel is a one-time job in CMMG's book, not part of cleaning, and is not in this guide.

steps.title: ⛔ Host unloaded and the ACTION OPEN before the can comes off
steps.action: Make the host firearm safe first: unloaded, with the action OPEN so you can see it is clear. CMMG asks for the action open specifically, every time the DEFCAN goes on or comes off.
steps.prose: Everything in this guide happens with a hand at the muzzle end. That is why the action stays open.
steps.quote: NOTE: Make sure firearm is unloaded and the action is open to verify clear before removing your DEFCAN from the host firearm.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.5

steps.title: ⛔ Let it COOL, or wear gloves
steps.action: Let the suppressor cool to the temperature of the room before you take it off or work on it. If it has to come off hot, wear protective gloves. Gloves also help at the mount, where the can and the muzzle device can pinch a finger as they come apart.
steps.prose: A rifle can after a string of fire is hot enough to burn badly, and it does not look hot.
steps.caution: The point of attachment or detachment can present the potential for pinching and caution should be taken, including wearing protective gloves, to avoid severe injury at the pinch point.
steps.quote: Allow suppressor to cool to ambient temperature before removal and/or service. If suppressor must be removed or installed while hot, protective gloves should be worn.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Safety notices, printed p.4

steps.title: Know the rating: both cans full-auto rated, with minimum barrel lengths
steps.action: Both DEFCANs are full-auto rated. CMMG sets a minimum barrel length for each: the DEFCAN-556 needs at least 6.5 inches of barrel in 5.56mm. The DEFCAN-762 needs at least 6.5 inches in 5.56mm and 12.5 inches in .308 Win, with no barrel-length restriction in 7.62x39mm.
steps.prose: Check the host against these numbers before the can goes back on, not after.
steps.quote: The DEFCAN-556 and DEFCAN-762 are both full auto rated.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Firing schedule, printed p.5

steps.title: Off the host, part 1: suppressor body counter-clockwise ONE turn
steps.action: Grip the suppressor body and unscrew it counter-clockwise one turn. This takes the tension off the lever-lock mount so the locking gate can be opened in the next step.
steps.prose: One turn only. You are slackening the mount, not taking the body off the mount.
steps.quote: Unscrew the suppressor body counter-clockwise 1 turn.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.5

steps.title: Off the host, part 2: release knob LEFT, locking gate UP, can off
steps.action: Push the locking release knob to the left and pull the locking gate upwards. The gate stops in its unlocked position. The DEFCAN then comes off the muzzle device. The ZEROED SVD brake or A2 flash hider stays on the barrel.
steps.prose: Mind the pinch point at the mount as the can comes away.
steps.aside: DEFCAN can be removed from the muzzle device.
steps.quote: Push the locking release knob to the left and pull the locking gate upwards. The locking gate will stop in its unlocked position.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Removal, printed p.5

steps.title: HUB mount off the body: DEFCAN spanner wrench, counter-clockwise
steps.action: Hold the DEFCAN body firmly in one hand. Line up the DEFCAN spanner wrench with the notches in the mount and turn it counter-clockwise to loosen, then unscrew the mount from the body. CMMG's regular maintenance includes cleaning the mount threads, the body threads and the blast chamber, and those surfaces are only reachable with the mount off.
steps.prose: The mount went on at 30 ft-lb, so expect it to need the wrench. Do not grip the can in a vise or use anything but the spanner on the mount's notches.
steps.aside: Firmly grasp the DEFCAN body in one hand.
steps.quote: Line up the DEFCAN spanner wrench with the notches in the mount and turn counter-clockwise to loosen.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — HUB Mount Removal, printed p.7

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes: the body is SEALED
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart. CMMG states that both DEFCANs are a sealed suppressor design: no front cap to remove and no baffle stack to pull. With the can off the host and the mount off the body, everything below is cleaning on a closed tube.
steps.prose: A sealed can is not a can you have failed to open. If something inside is wrong, it goes back to CMMG.
steps.quote: Both DEFCAN-556 and DEFCAN-762 are a sealed suppressor design, eliminating much of the disassembly required for general cleaning and maintenance such as the front cap and inner baffles
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: Inspect it: bore, a shake, the outside
steps.action: Look through the bore for any obstruction or foreign object. Shake the can and listen for anything broken or loose inside. On a sealed can that is the only internal check you have. Then check the outside for dents or other damage. CMMG wants this before and after every use.
steps.prose: A rattle, a blocked bore or a dented tube means the can does not go back on the rifle until CMMG has seen it.
steps.aside: Visually inspect the bore of the suppressor for any obstructions or foreign objects.
steps.quote: Shake the suppressor and listen to check for any broken or detached internal parts.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: Mount, threads and blast chamber: clean and lightly oil
steps.action: With the mount off, clean the QD mount's surfaces and threads, the suppressor body's threads, and the blast chamber, then put a light coat of oil on them. Carbon on these surfaces is what turns a solid lockup into play.
steps.prose: Light oil means light. The threads get anti-seize when the mount goes back in.
steps.quote: Remove, clean, and lightly oil the QD mount surfaces and threads as well as the suppressor body threads and blast chamber.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: Bore: brush and solvent, NEVER a patch
steps.action: Use a bore brush and gun cleaning solvent to take carbon buildup and fouling out of the suppressor bore. Do not run a cleaning patch through it: a patch can lodge inside the sealed can and cause damage the next time the rifle is fired. Do not put the can in an ultrasonic cleaner either; CMMG says it can damage the finish.
steps.prose: The brush comes back out on the rod. A patch has nothing holding it.
steps.caution: NOTE: Suppressor should NOT be cleaned in an ultrasonic cleaner. Damage to finish may occur.
steps.quote: A bore brush and gun cleaning solvent may be used to remove any carbon buildup or fouling from the bore of the suppressor.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6
steps.warn: NOTE: Do NOT run cleaning patches through the bore of the suppressor as they could become lodged inside the suppressor and cause damage upon firing.

steps.title: Stubborn buildup: soak, then stand it HUB-threads DOWN to drain
steps.action: For buildup the brush will not shift, CMMG allows a solvent soak with the QD mount off the body. Afterwards stand the can on a clean towel with the HUB threaded end down and the front cap up, so standing solvent runs down the baffle stack and out through the bore hole. Let it dry completely before anything is oiled or put back together.
steps.prose: Solvent left inside a sealed can has nowhere to go but out the muzzle the next time you fire it. Give it the time to drain and dry.
steps.aside: Allow the suppressor to completely dry before lightly oiling surfaces, applying anti-seize to threads, and re-assembling.
steps.quote: If soaking the suppressor in solvent to remove stubborn buildup, remove the QD mount from the body and stand the suppressor up on a clean towel with the HUB threaded side facing down and front cap facing up to allow any standing solvent to run down the baffle stack and drain through the bore hole.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — General maintenance & cleaning, printed p.6

steps.title: If it has been in water: drain, flush hot, dry, oil
steps.action: Do this as soon as you can after the can has been used in or exposed to water. Let it drain completely. Soak and flush it with very hot water and detergent, draining between rounds, three to four times at least. Then flush it with clean boiling water. Dry it with compressed air through the can if you have it, or overnight in an oven on a warm setting if time allows. Once it is thoroughly dry, lubricate the mount and threads.
steps.prose: Do not shoot it wet unless you truly have to. CMMG's word is absolutely necessary.
steps.aside: After the suppressor has been thoroughly dried, lubricate the mount and threads.
steps.quote: Soak and flush the suppressor with very hot water and a detergent. Drain and repeat this procedure a minimum of 3-4 times.
steps.cite: CMMG DEFCAN-556 / DEFCAN-762 — OWNER'S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — the text layer carries no revision or date code — Maintenance after water exposure, printed p.7
steps.warn: Allow to drain completely and DO NOT use the suppressor unless absolutely necessary.

deepAbsentReason: CMMG's book calls both the DEFCAN-556 and the DEFCAN-762 a sealed suppressor design (printed p.6): the front cap and inner baffles do not come apart, and the book prints no procedure that opens the body. The deepest work it publishes is taking the HUB mount off the body with the DEFCAN spanner wrench, a solvent soak, and the flush after water exposure (printed pp.6–7). CMMG makes those part of its regular maintenance, and they are in the routine lane above. A can that rattles, is blocked or is damaged goes back to CMMG: the book asks the owner to contact CMMG Customer Service for a return authorization and not to return it to the retailer (printed p.9). This listing therefore has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: INSPECTION — BEFORE AND AFTER USE
tasks: Look through the bore for obstructions or foreign objects.
Shake the can and listen for anything broken or detached inside.
Check the outside for dents or other damage.

cleaning.name: MOUNT, THREADS & BLAST CHAMBER
tasks: QD mount off the body with the DEFCAN spanner wrench, counter-clockwise.
Clean the mount's surfaces and threads, the body threads and the blast chamber.
A light coat of oil on those surfaces.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bore brush and gun cleaning solvent for carbon and fouling.
⛔ Never run a cleaning patch through the bore.
Do not clean the can in an ultrasonic cleaner.

cleaning.name: SOLVENT SOAK & DRY
tasks: Only for stubborn buildup, with the QD mount off the body.
Stand it on a clean towel, HUB threads down, front cap up, to drain.
Completely dry before oiling, anti-seize or reassembly.

cleaning.name: AFTER WATER EXPOSURE
tasks: As soon as possible: drain completely.
Very hot water and detergent, soak and flush, at least 3–4 times.
A flush with clean boiling water.
Dry with compressed air, or overnight in an oven on warm.
Lubricate the mount and threads once thoroughly dry.

reassembly: Mount surfaces and threads clean; a light coat of oil on the mount surfaces and a thin coat of anti-seize on the threads.
Thread the mount into the DEFCAN body clockwise by hand, taking care not to cross-thread it.
Once hand tight, use the DEFCAN wrench on a 3/8" drive torque wrench to tighten the mount to 30 ft-lb.
Host firearm unloaded, with the action open to verify clear.
Push the locking release knob to the left and pull the locking gate up to its unlocked position; unscrew the suppressor body counter-clockwise 1 turn.
Slide the DEFCAN over the ZEROED SVD brake or mil-spec A2 flash hider, with the locking gate matching the wrench flats on the muzzle device.
Push the locking gate down until it is completely seated and the locking release knob engages.
Grip the suppressor body and turn it clockwise until the slack is taken up. Hand seated is enough: do not tighten it further once no play is felt or heard.
fncheck: With the host firearm unloaded and the action open: the locking gate is fully down with the release knob engaged, and the body is turned clockwise hand-snug. Try to move the can by hand. CMMG's test is that no play is felt or heard, and the can should not be tightened past that point. Look through the bore for obstructions, shake the can and listen for anything loose inside, and check the mount turned in to 30 ft-lb if it was off the body.
